title: 1.1 Continental Drift Theory
description: Pangaea, Laurasia, Gondwanaland, and the geological evidence behind Wegener’s theory. Medium level.

questions.question: What does the continental drift theory propose about continents?
options: They have moved relative to each other over geologic time
They have remained fixed in place
They rotate only around the poles
questions.correctAnswer: They have moved relative to each other over geologic time

questions.question: Which fossil reptile, about 250 million years old, supported Wegener’s theory?
Which type of evidence uses ancient climate data reconstructed from rocks?
Why was Wegener’s theory rejected partly because of his background?
options: He worked only in the Southern Hemisphere
He was a meteorologist turned geologist
He was not a geologist by profession
questions.correctAnswer: He was not a geologist by profession

questions.question: Where were most influential geoscientists based at the time?
What was the greatest unresolved problem in Wegener’s theory?
options: The lack of a plausible mechanism for continental movement
questions.correctAnswer: The lack of a plausible mechanism for continental movement

questions.question: Until which era did Wegener believe Pangaea remained intact?
How did matching mountain belts in Africa and South America support the theory?
options: They proved a volcanic origin for both continents
They showed the continents evolved separately
They suggested the continents were once joined
questions.correctAnswer: They suggested the continents were once joined

questions.question: What idea introduced by Wegener’s work shifted thinking from fixism?
Which present-day continent was largely part of Gondwanaland?
